first_prompt: Review and implement `~/code/scripts/analysis/brief-generation-quality-takeaway.md`. The last few runs have gone quite well, so be aspirational with how you approach the work to maximize quality and e

commits.summary: Give the brief author four rules for each case, and count what a brief shows of them
commits.body:
The user compared six generated briefs (155 cases) with rationale files of their own, which stay private, and wrote the result up as llm-dlc/loops/brief-generation-quality-takeaway.md. The brief author misread and missed nothing, but in every batch it dropped or blurred the second observation that changes one input, three times accepted "either order" where the behaviour defines an order, and reached for a database, JMS or a child process where a public call would show the same. Its own predictions that the merged code is still wrong were a strength worth keeping. The rate did not vary with the size of the list, so the gap is in the instructions. This is now VF-075 in verification/findings.md, with the cause, what landed, the baseline and what the user's next comparison should count.

llm-dlc/loops/brief-generation-template.md gives the author four rules for each case, in the first text in full and in the continue message in short (a later cycle starts after a compaction with the continue message alone): a claim row with the role Variation that repeats the main observation with exactly one input changed and says what each revision should do, the reversal where the behaviour depends on order; the order stated and checked wherever the code under change produces one; the cheapest observation that shows the change, with the reason in the technical notes when more than a public call is needed; and a claim row with the role Remaining defect wherever the landed code still looks wrong. The two are claim rows because the agent that verifies a brief decides every claim row. The author checks the rules before a cycle ends and gives its counts with "The brief is complete" and in its record. The user's handoff is unchanged, and single_run.py renders the template as before.

brief_queue.py counts what a written brief shows of the rules: the cases with a Variation row and those without, the Remaining defect rows, and the cases whose words leave an order open. The brief step of next gives the count when it queues a generated brief (caseRules, a line for the user, the queue's log) and refuses nothing; brief_queue.py rules FILE counts any brief. Over the nine generated briefs on the line (235 cases) it finds no such rows, as the roles did not exist, and 13 cases that leave an order open. The single-agent-run skill page describes the rules and the count for the watcher.

Verified by tests of the texts an author is given, not of the template file: both texts as generate renders them hold each rule (they lacked all four before the change, in both); the text the Codex stand-in was started with and the run's continue message hold them; and so do the first and the continued prompt of an author the queue started, whose brief the brief step then counts. python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py run --changed passed 7 of 7 test files, and the lint of the test inventory agrees (two new unit rows). Nothing here runs a prover, so there is no verification job. Not shown yet: that an author follows the rules, which the user's comparison of the next generated list with a rationale file will show.

commits.summary: Add the register of what is retired, and a check that live files point at it
commits.body:
The user decided on 2026-11-27 that the project converges on one run skill, to be called orchestrate-run, and that every other proof workflow is outdated: multi-agent-brief, the proof loop behind prove-java-change, the loops started by hand, the Sonnet verification loop, and the published plugin with its runtime mode. Nothing is to leave the history of work, and whatever names a retired thing is to say where to find it.

llm-dlc/retired.md is that place: one entry for each thing, with what it was, what replaced it, the names that should no longer turn up in live files, the files that go, and the change that removed it. Every entry is still planned: this change removes nothing. llm-dlc/tools/retired.py reads the entries and lists each paragraph of a live file (instructions, skills, tools and their tests) that names something retired without pointing at the register, and each retired file that is still here. test_retired.py runs it on the repository, so it starts to hold as entries turn retired. With --planned it shows the work ahead: 367 paragraphs in 72 live files and 39 files.

Verified by test_retired.py (5 tests: an entry's form, a failing page and its control once it points at the register, names as whole words, a retired file still present, the generated table of sessions left unread) and by test_costs.py lint. The inventory also gains the rows of nine tests other sessions added without them.

commits.summary: Move what the run tools share out of the two controllers that are being retired
commits.body:
single_run.py and brief_queue.py took landing, trial merges, queue keeping, the nested-run refusal and the clock from brief_run.py (the streams' controller) and watch.py (the proof run's), which are to be retired (llm-dlc/retired.md). Their text is moved, unchanged, into three modules: run_common.py (a run's state, the clock, what a turn cost, jj, the workspaces and loops of a folder, the commits a run made, the refusal to start a run from inside one), landing.py (land, onto_line, trial_merge and the locks they hold) and queue_keeping.py (collect, start_runner, tend). The two old controllers import them, so both still work as before; single_run.py and brief_queue.py no longer import either controller. One wording differs: a merge landed with no message of its own now names the workspace, and the foundation stage passes its own words.

watch.py had also become the home of checks on examples. They move to examples/tools: preflight.py (what each example named lacks before a run takes it; validate_example.py and the numbered handoff call it) and observe.py (the startup-facts and public-observation reports). watch.py's commands of those names call them. preflight.py no longer says which claims a person has reviewed: that record belongs to the proof run, and watch.py adds it for as long as it exists.

Verified by the changed-tests run: 66 of 66 test files passed, among them the two old controllers' own (test_brief_run 54, test_watch 42, test_prove_loop 32), test_single_run (29) and test_brief_queue (12). The moved code has tests of its own that do not go through a retiring controller: test_landing.py (14, on real jj repositories: forward, merge, conflict taken back, another session's files, trace output, a person's decisions, onto_line, a trial merge), test_queue_keeping.py (6), test_run_common.py (9) and test_preflight.py (9). The cost lint agrees.

commits.summary: Rename the run skill to orchestrate-run, with a page for each kind of run
commits.body:
The user decided on 2026-11-27 that the project converges on one run skill and named it orchestrate-run. It is single-agent-run under a new name: its commands (single_run.py, brief_queue.py) and a run's folder (single-NAME) are unchanged, so no record changes.

The one page of 388 lines is now a core page and four beside it. SKILL.md holds what every run needs: the watcher's rules, the request, a run under way, start, watch and report, and a table of the four kinds of run. setup.md, generation.md, queue.md and redaction.md hold the sections of those names, moved as they were, and the core page tells the watcher to read a kind's page in full before acting on it and again after a compaction. The opening no longer describes the watcher by two skills that are being retired; it says this is the repository's one run skill and points at llm-dlc/retired.md for the others.

The by-hand resolution of a landing that conflicts was written only on the proof run's page, which is to be retired: it is now in the operating notes ("A landing that conflicts"), and the skill and landing.py's message point there. The register's entry for single-agent-run is retired, and the check holds for it: no live file names the old skill without pointing at the register.

Verified by the changed-tests run (60 of 60 test files, among them test_agent_client, whose list of the run skills that are the user's alone in Codex now names orchestrate-run), and by agent_client.py instructions --client codex, which finds every skill linked and reports no problem.

commits.summary: Retire the streams workflow: /multi-agent-brief, brief_run.py and run-streams.sh
commits.body:
The user decided on 2026-11-27 that the project converges on one run skill, /orchestrate-run, and that every other proof workflow is outdated. This removes the workflow that ran a brief as parallel streams: the skill multi-agent-brief, its controller brief_run.py, run-streams.sh with its status bar (streams_status.py), the streams' inboxes (inbox.py), the rolling integration line (integration.py and the four briefs' integration scripts), transfer-session.sh, and the four test files of those tools. Nothing is removed from the history: llm-dlc/retired.md names the change that removed them, and its parent is the last commit that has them. The entry also says where the foundation session's prompt, the user's text, is to be read.

What the surviving tools shared with that workflow was moved out two commits ago (run_common.py, landing.py, queue_keeping.py) and is unchanged here. The rest is wording: the conductor no longer describes the two questions only streams asked (their three answers are still read, so an old run directory's verdicts are), feature-loop.sh no longer ends a brief's instruction with the sentence that pointed at an inbox no tool writes, and llm-dlc/README.md's section on a brief's run is replaced by a short one that points at the register and keeps the three things it said that hold for every run. The operating notes keep the user's rule about sessions beside a run.

One thing the removal makes visible, and does not fix: only the default workspace publishes run records, and run-streams.sh was the one caller of run_records.py, which copies a workspace's records there. No command of a single run does that, so no single run's record is published and the loop statistics count none (llm-dlc/traces/loops.md names no single-NAME run). The pages now say so. Copying them at a landing would publish some dozens of records at once and is for the user to decide.

Verified by the changed-tests run (32 of 32 test files, among them test_single_run 29, test_brief_queue 12, test_prove_loop 32, test_watch 42, test_conductor 23, test_agent_client 27, test_landing 14, test_queue_keeping 6) and by retired.py check, which finds no retired file still here and no live paragraph that names the streams' tools without pointing at the register. The cost inventory drops the 77 rows of the removed tests, and its lint agrees.

commits.summary: Retire the proof loop, the loops by hand and the verification loop
commits.body:
The second removal of the convergence on /orchestrate-run (the user's decision of 2026-11-27; llm-dlc/retired.md). It removes the proof run of a development checkout (watch.py, prove-loop.sh, the watcher's summary template, the plan template, the links that offered /prove-java-change here) and the verification loop (verification-loop.sh), with their three test files. Nothing is removed from the history: the register names this change, and its parent is the last commit with those files.

feature-loop.sh is now the loop under a run and nothing else: 755 lines where it had 1,450. It ran four kinds of loop, and three are retired with this change (moonshots by name, templated moonshots over examples with their judge, items and waiting, and briefs by name or file with their settings, status line and decision turn). The single-agent kind is unchanged line for line, and the script refuses the other names with a pointer to the register. The conductor loses the two questions only the proof loop asked and its matching of jobs to examples; its answers are still read, so an old run directory's verdicts are. The watcher of a run no longer defers to a verification loop or to another kind of run for the queue: it keeps it whenever its run says so.

The compaction watch, the handling of a scope left by an ended loop, the refusal of a loop inside a loop and the private copy of the script were tested only through the proof loop. test_feature_loop.py now tests them on the single-agent loop (9 tests, the script run for real against a stand-in client), with one for the refusal of a retired kind.

Kept, though the proof run used them: prove-plan.schema.json (the scaffold and one study write and read the format), changes.py and doctor.py (the surviving tools call them). The published plugin's skill and llm-dlc/runtime.md still describe the proof run: they belong to the release the plugin pins, are exempt from the register's check by name, and go with the plugin in the next change. Three studies that pinned the tools of the revision they ran on still name retired files and are left as records; they read those files from that revision.

Verified: the changed-tests run passed 29 of 32 test files, and the three that failed were fixed and pass alone (test_single_run 29 and test_brief_queue 12, which need the line single_run.py looks for in the script, now kept; test_claude_setup 21, an assertion on a message this change reworded). retired.py check finds nothing, and the cost lint agrees.

commits.summary: Retire the published plugin and runtime mode
commits.body:
The last removal of the convergence on /orchestrate-run, which the user decided on 2026-11-27 and asked to be done last (llm-dlc/retired.md). It removes the plugin in-the-loop with its skill /prove-java-change, its bootstrap and the pin of release 0.10.0, the marketplace entry, the page of runtime mode (llm-dlc/runtime.md), and the tools that existed for a released copy on a user's machine: release.py, mode.py, claude_setup.py and contribute.py, with their four test files. Nothing is removed from the history: the register names this change, and its parent is the last commit with those files. Nothing replaces the product yet; the register says so.

The repository now has one mode. sync.py no longer asks which mode a checkout is in and loses its plain-commit branch; it still reads the In-The-Loop-Runtime trailer, because commits contributed from a released copy are in the history and must never be stamped with a session. The loop no longer starts sessions with the flags of a clean launch, which only a runtime checkout used, and the conductor no longer keeps a decision record under a local name. changes.py and doctor.py are kept and described without the plugin.

CLAUDE.md describes one mode, gains a short section on runs that names /orchestrate-run and points at the register, and no longer speaks of a release as a point where the default run is owed, or of streams. The front page (README.md) is an interim one, to be restructured with the user: it says what the repository is, how work is run, and that the plugin is retired, and keeps the sections on the three answers, the layout and the background.

Left as records: the benchmark of external upgrades measured the plugin at pinned revisions, and its operator harness names the plugin's files; it needs a new product entry before it can measure a later revision. The register says so.

Verified by the changed-tests run (51 of 51 test files, among them test_single_run 29, test_feature_loop 9, test_conductor 20, test_performance 114, test_review 37 and test_changes 22), by sync.py check, which the commit itself runs on the new sync.py, by agent_client.py instructions --client codex (no problem, every skill linked), and by retired.py check: no retired file is still here and no live paragraph names one without pointing at the register. The check's three exemptions for the plugin's pages are removed with them.

That commit's message says the check reported no problem. It did report this one: the command printed it and exited 0, and the commit was made in the same line without the output being read.

CLAUDE.md now names the skill without its page and says its pages are for the watcher a person starts, and points at llm-dlc/README.md for how a run goes. The queue was held throughout, so no run met the refusal.

test_agent_client.py gains a unit test that fails when CLAUDE.md names the page of a skill only a person starts, so the next such link is found before a commit. Verified: agent_client.py instructions --client codex reports no problem and lists only run-verification to a work turn; test_agent_client passes (28 tests); the cost lint and retired.py check agree.

commits.summary: Restructure the front page around results, with a way in for a reader
commits.body:
The front page was an interim one since the plugin was retired. The user chose its structure on 2026-11-27: results first, one status line for the retired plugin, a round figure for the examples with a link to the generated router, a way to reproduce one result, and a short section on how the repository is built with a placeholder for an architecture diagram.

README.md now runs: what this is; the three answers and example 285; what is here; how to explore it with an agent or reproduce a result, and what that takes; how it is built; status; for agents; background; licence. The section on exploring says how the artifacts link (an example to its result, a job to the session that submitted it and the commit it ran on, a commit to its session and log, a session to its summary, metrics and transcript), since everything is public and a coding agent can follow the links from a checkout. The hardware note gives the minimums and comfortable figures doctor.py holds, and says that running the workflow itself needs a large machine and is for people who want to work on the verifier. The count of examples was stale (183; there are 515, 305 of them real-world): the page now says more than 500 and links the router, whose tables are generated.

Verified: python3 examples/tools/build.py 002 was run once under a memory and time cap and ended with the line the page quotes, in 16 seconds; the files it rewrote were put back. The other claims were checked against the files they describe (a job's submitted.session, a result's sourceCommit, a summary's link to its log, the pipeline's max_timeout). The changed-tests run passed 38 of 38 test files, and retired.py check finds nothing.

commits.summary: Point the historical pages and findings that name something retired at the register
commits.body:
The user's decision of 2026-11-27 for the convergence on /orchestrate-run: live files are rewritten, records are never edited, and a historical page that names something retired keeps its text and gets one dated line that points at llm-dlc/retired.md. This adds that line to the 38 pages of llm-dlc/loops that name a retired skill, command or script (the briefs of earlier loops and their streams, results pages, the brief template of that time) and to the 11 entries of verification/findings.md that do. Each line says what the page names, the change that removed it, and the register entry that says what replaced it. The 6 pages there that the queue's log names, its copies of the user's briefs, are records and are untouched.

retired.py writes the lines from the register's entries (banners --write) and its check now fails on a historical page or a finding that lacks one, so the next retirement is one command and a page added later is caught by the default test run. The fixtures' pages under lib/tests are held to the live rule, and the two that sent a reader to an integration script now say it went with the streams workflow.

VF-045 and VF-072 each gain a dated note of what the convergence changed for them: one run skill is left and is the user's alone to start in Codex, the refusal of a run started inside a loop moved to run_common.py, and CLAUDE.md names the skill without its page, which a test now holds. Neither is closed: what the agents wanted (fan-out, sealed producers, a worker request) is untouched.

Verified: test_retired.py passes (9 tests, 4 of them new: the line a page and a finding lack, that it is written once and a record is left alone, a line that names two changes, and this repository's own pages); retired.py check finds nothing; the changed-tests run passed 22 of 22 test files; the cost lint agrees.

commits.summary: Operating notes: what a session from before the one run skill has to drop
commits.body:
On 2026-11-27 the repository converged on one run skill, /orchestrate-run (llm-dlc/retired.md). A watcher that was started before that day, a compacted session or a client's own memory may still hold the older names, and the user asked that the watcher update its memory and procedures from the change before the queue resumes.

The operating notes, which every agent reads, now open with a section for that reader: the skill's new name and its split into pages, the commands that did not change, what is gone with nothing to call in its place, what moved (the example checks of the proof run's tool), that the watcher keeps the queue itself and defers to no other kind of run, and that a procedure of its own which names an old command is checked against the register before it is acted on.

Verified: retired.py check finds nothing (each paragraph of the section that names something retired points at the register), and the changed-tests run passed 3 of 3 test files.

commits.summary: The register's check: a folder that keeps only a bytecode cache is gone
commits.body:
The user's whole default test run on the default line (xksklxrk) failed on 2026-11-27 at 18:30 UTC. Its output was not kept, and the cause found afterwards is test_retired.py: retired.py check said `plugins/` was still here, though the change that retired the plugin had removed every file it tracked. The folder held one file, the bytecode cache Python had written when a test imported the plugin's bootstrap. jj removes the files it tracks and leaves what it ignores, so any checkout that ran those tests before the removal keeps such a folder; a workspace where the folder was removed by hand, as the one the removal was made in, does not, which is why the tests passed there.

A retired folder now counts as still here by the files in it, and a file under __pycache__ (or a .pyc) is not one; an empty folder is not either. A link still counts, whatever it points at. Two tests hold this: a folder with only a cache is gone, and one with a file of its own is reported.

Also: the headers of two Rust tests still said an integration script runs them; they now say it went with the streams workflow, and lib/tests/*.rs is held to the rule for live files.

Verified: test_retired.py passes (11 tests) and the two Rust test binaries pass (12 and 5 tests) in the changed-tests run; the fixed check, pointed at the default checkout's files while the leftover folder was there, reported nothing; the old check in the default checkout failed on it and passes once the folder is removed, which was done (it held that one cache file and nothing tracked). The whole default run on the tree before this fix passed in this workspace, 85 of 85; one on the tree with it follows.

commits.summary: VF-078: a run's reported spend is short, and a workspace's run is in no published record
commits.body:
Two gaps found while converging the run skills on /orchestrate-run, recorded for whoever next works on run records. Neither came with that work and it fixed neither.

A run's reported spend counts a cycle when its question is put to the watcher, so a cycle that ends the run with no question, the last compact and the summary are left out: a rehearsal of the tools reported 0.19 dollars where the client's total for the session was 0.63. And the records of a run that worked in a workspace of its own are published nowhere, since only the default workspace's are and nothing copies them there since the streams workflow was retired: the workspace the queue's runs work in holds 91 such records, the default checkout none, and the loop statistics count no single run.

The entry is the rehearsal's only record: the run was made in a throwaway copy on Claude Opus 5.5 at low effort, and the copy and its transcript were deleted afterwards at the user's wish.

Verified: retired.py check finds nothing in the new entry, and the changed-tests run passed 6 of 6 test files. The findings page is one no test of the default run reads, so the passed run recorded for the tree before this commit still covers it.

commits.summary: VF-079: a session's trace line lands on commits it did not make
commits.body:
Recorded for the user's decision. sync.py takes a session to have made every mutable ancestor of @ dated while it ran, and @ itself while it is live, so a line can land on a commit another session or a person made. It was seen twice during the convergence on /orchestrate-run and came with neither.

First, the convergence's first commit put its session's line on three unpublished commits under it, two allow-list proposals and the user's own approval; each now names three sessions. Second, a sync of this session run in another workspace, merge-fixes, by a session with an uncommitted change that renders a session from another workspace's transcript, gave that workspace's working-copy change this session's line and stored the log it names there alone. That failed the check of the commit before this one in this workspace (log 614ccbcc12c9 neither stored locally nor uploaded); sync.py adopt-logs brought the log over and the check is back at 0 errors.

The entry puts two readings of a trace line to the user and asks that, under either, a session rendered from another workspace's transcript is not given the rendering checkout's working copy. No trace line was edited.

Verified: retired.py check finds nothing in the entry, and the changed-tests run passed 6 of 6 test files. The findings page is one no test of the default run reads, so the passed whole run recorded for the tree at qvsumqom still covers this commit.

commits.summary: Let sync SESSION re-render a session whose transcript is in another workspace's folder
commits.body: On 2026-11-27 the merge of the promotion's record with the line conflicted in the Fable session's manifest: the promotion marked an earlier log uploaded, and the line added a later log. The way to settle such a conflict is to re-render the manifest with sync.py sync SESSION, but transcript_of looked only in this checkout's project folder and its own Codex rollouts, and the Fable transcript is in the queue workspace's folder, so the watcher could not settle it. transcript_of now falls back to the transcript wherever it is on this machine (transcript_anywhere, which VF-074's fix added), never a Codex thread that was only asked a question. A session rendered from another workspace's transcript keeps the workspace its manifest names, whose paths its log has, instead of taking this checkout's; its summary is rendered by that workspace as well. The size total in traces/README.md now counts a log this workspace does not store yet as 0 instead of failing, which a re-render of such a session met. The way to settle the conflict: restore the side whose manifest records the upload (jj restore --from that side the manifest), then sync.py adopt-logs and sync.py sync SESSION, which adds the later log and keeps the URL. Verified: a unit test (a transcript in another workspace's folder is found and is not this checkout's own; with none anywhere the old name is kept); a real sync of the Fable session from a fresh workspace found its transcript, kept its workspace and added its later log after adopt-logs; test_costs run --changed, 23 of 23 files pass; lint agrees.

commits.summary: Record VF-077: gaps in the redaction review, from an outside review of the open findings
commits.body: At the user's request (2026-11-27), from a review by an agent outside this checkout of all 214 open findings against their real values and the 418 published logs. No credential or secret is among them: the 66 proposals and the rest are test, build and run output. One real miss, 56b88bc7, a base64 file: URL under the home folder from a threetenbp run in Codex session 01a20c2d-af08, is already in 58 published logs and exposes only the public account name; the reviewer recommends accepting it. The entry records the process gaps that matter more: a person's pane captured into a published log while sync.py allow printed values unmasked (2026-11-23), no review of findings that exist only in published logs, a line-by-line redactor that misses wrapped values, no match for encoded personal values, and ambiguous eight-character session ids in review. It names the decisions that are the user's and a fix for each gap.

commits.summary: VF-077: add the watcher's account of the gaps
commits.body: The queue's watcher (6c5c7798) added its own account. All 214 open findings are now proposed. It captured the user's pane during allow approve on 2026-11-23, which produced 14 long-token findings in its log, each appearing 586 times. A masking step of its own printed a 29-character fragment again on 2026-11-27, under the 40-character threshold. review show is too slow, and shows too little context for some families to classify them, which made an outside pass necessary before a promotion. Agents have no read-only way to see allow's usage, since sync.py push ignores --help. The entry adds those as gaps 6 and 7, with fixes.

commits.summary: VF-077: the user's direction for sensitive commands
commits.body: The user, 2026-11-27: sensitive commands go in a separate tmux session that agents never read, and everything else stays in the user's usual session, so agents can help and watch work finish. A command that can be made less sensitive without losing its function should be: for example, masked values by default in allow and allow approve, with an explicit flag to unmask. Commands whose output may hold real values are designated sensitive (in their usage, and with a notice when run outside a terminal of their own), so it's clear where each one runs.

commits.summary: ARCHITECTURE.md: the map of who owns what, who may do what and what is not built
commits.body:
The user asked for the architecture page to become a first-class file of the project once the run skills had converged, written from their draft and updated to the implementation and the direction as they now are. This is its first version, at the repository's root, for their review.

The page has one path (a person, a watcher, a run, its jobs, a checker, the line, develop, main) with a diagram, the four kinds of run, where the judgment is and where it is not, a table of owners with each one's contract, a table of who may do what and what holds each rule, the record that answers each question, and one section for what is intended and not built: a product entry, the job pipeline the user wants to grow out of /run-verification, fan-out from a manifest, a sealed producer, a worker request, the filter-stop wording, machine-wide run visibility, a run's record and cost (VF-078), the meaning of a trace line (VF-079), network capacity. It also says how a finding becomes the next plan, how something is retired, and how the page is kept. Against the draft: the released product and its mode, the streams' controller and the proof run's watcher are gone from the owners, links are relative so that they resolve at the commit being read, and measurements are left with their owners.

Held by two checks in the default run: test_architecture.py fails when a link of ARCHITECTURE.md or README.md leads to a file or a heading that is not in the repository (with a made-up page as its control), and the register's check now reads the page as a live file. The front page's placeholder becomes a small diagram and a link to the page, and CLAUDE.md gains a section that sends an agent to it before it adds a tool or moves a responsibility, and has it updated in the same commit.

Verified: test_architecture.py passes (4 tests) and so does the changed-tests run, 40 of 40 test files; retired.py check finds nothing; agent_client.py instructions --client codex reports no problem with the longer CLAUDE.md (read, not chained); both diagrams were rendered once with Mermaid 10.9.1 in the headless browser and came out with the nodes and edges written (8 and 11, 6 and 5).

The test inventory merged without one.

commits.summary: Add a read-only audit of the job records, with the pinned corpus as its fixture
commits.body:
First slice of the brief for one jobs pipeline (llm-dlc/loops/in-the-loop-generic-jobs-pipeline-brief.md), its gate 'protect and measure'. jobs/records.py reads the committed specifications and receipts by job id, from a git revision (git objects alone) or from a working copy, and computes the result indexes from the receipts. jobs/audit.py joins specifications, receipts, what each receipt names in its own folder, the indexes and, for a working copy, the runner's claims and staged results. It reports a discrepancy where two records of one job cannot both be right (exit 1), a gap where a record names something the revision does not hold, and a note for a fact of the layout. It can write and verify a manifest of the paths and git ids of every specification, receipt and result folder. verification/pipeline.py now writes the indexes with the function the audit recomputes them with. The retirement check reads the new jobs/ folder as live code and pages.

The corpus at b52a084f5d11 is frozen as jobs/fixtures/census-b52a084f5d11.json and manifest-b52a084f5d11.jsonl.gz (1,906 rows, 32,071 files). It has 1,906 job ids with a specification, a receipt and an index row each, 1,469 passed, 420 failed and 17 error, three flat specifications of 2026-11-22 with a result under their day, no discrepancy, and seven index files that the receipts give back to the byte. The audit also found 947 kept outputs of 19 jobs that receipts name and no commit holds, 945 under an ignored path and 2 over the commit limit, none sealed as an original; 944 are still on disk in the default checkout. That is recorded as VF-080.

Verified: jobs/test_audit.py, 16 tests (a made-up corpus with one fault at a time, the pinned corpus against its census and its manifest at the pinned revision and at this commit); verification/test_pipeline.py, 48 tests; the tests of what changed, 30 of 30 files; retired.py check finds nothing; the cost lint agrees.
